# 01 Data preparation

## Datasets used for this project

Under 5 mortality rate: <https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/under-five-mortality-rate-(probability-of-dying-by-age-5-per-1000-live-births)>

Measles vaccine: <https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/measles-containing-vaccine-first-dose-(mcv1)-immunization-coverage-among-1-year-olds-(-)>

Stuntng prevalence:

<https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/gho-jme-country-children-aged-5-years-stunted-(-height-for-age--2-sd)>\

## Load libraries

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("here")
library("patchwork") # don't know if this is needed really
```

## Prepare datasets

Turn csv files into dataframes:

```{r}
# Under 5 mortality rate
under_5_mortality_rate <- read_csv(file = here("data/raw/under_5_mortality_rate.csv"))

# Measles vaccine
measles_vaccine <- read_csv(file = here("data/raw/measles_vaccine.csv"))

# Stunting prevalence
stunting_prevalence <- read_csv(file = here("data/raw/stunting_prevalence.csv"))
```

## Data wrangling

For each dataset we keep only the variables we need (ISO3 country code, country name, WHO region, year and the value), give them consistent snake_case names and make sure the value is numeric. The result has one row per country and year.

### Under 5 mortality rate

The raw file has one row per country, year *and sex* (`Female`, `Male`, `Both sexes`, stored in `Dim1`). We keep only `Both sexes` before dropping the sex variable, otherwise every country-year would appear three times.

`Value` is a string with the estimate and its CI, e.g. "1.1 \[0.5-2.5\]", so we use `str_extract()` from stringr to keep only the first number.

```{r}
under_5_mortality_rate_clean <- under_5_mortality_rate |>
  filter(Dim1 == "Both sexes") |>
  mutate(under_5_mortality = as.numeric(str_extract(Value, "^[0-9.]+"))) |>
  select(country_code = SpatialDimValueCode,
         country = Location,
         who_region = ParentLocation,
         year = Period,
         under_5_mortality) |>
  arrange(country_code, year)
```

### Measles vaccine

`Value` is already numeric (% of 1-year-olds with the first MCV dose), so we only select and rename.

```{r}
measles_vaccine_clean <- measles_vaccine |>
  select(country_code = SpatialDimValueCode,
         country = Location,
         who_region = ParentLocation,
         year = Period,
         mcv1_coverage = Value) |>
  arrange(country_code, year)
```

### Stunting prevalence

`Value` again combines the estimate with the CI, e.g. "17.4 \[16.7-18.3\]", but some rows have no CI (e.g. "10.5"). The same `str_extract()` pattern handles both. Here `year` is the survey year, so countries only have rows for the years a survey was done.

```{r}
stunting_prevalence_clean <- stunting_prevalence |>
  mutate(stunting_prevalence = as.numeric(str_extract(Value, "^[0-9.]+"))) |>
  select(country_code = SpatialDimValueCode,
         country = Location,
         who_region = ParentLocation,
         year = Period,
         stunting_prevalence) |>
  arrange(country_code, year)
```

### Check the tidy datasets

```{r}
glimpse(under_5_mortality_rate_clean)
glimpse(measles_vaccine_clean)
glimpse(stunting_prevalence_clean)
```

## Save processed data

The tidy datasets are saved as R objects (`.rds`) in `data/processed/`, so the other documents can load them directly, e.g. `read_rds(here("data/processed/measles_vaccine.rds"))`.

```{r}
dir.create(here("data/processed"), showWarnings = FALSE)

write_rds(under_5_mortality_rate_clean, here("data/processed/under_5_mortality_rate.rds"))
write_rds(measles_vaccine_clean, here("data/processed/measles_vaccine.rds"))
write_rds(stunting_prevalence_clean, here("data/processed/stunting_prevalence.rds"))
```
